why_relevant: Business daily with a dedicated banking-and-finance desk; publishes on acquiring, payment terminals, merchant contracts and bank technology suppliers — deal-level detail rarely available in English. Confirmed article on merchants cancelling payment-terminal contracts as terminal counts fell.

Czech internet/ICT trade server; runs a dedicated series on how the state awards digital/IT public contracts (co-produced with ASWA, the software agencies association) plus sustained BankID and internet-banking coverage. Topic hub pages act as ready-made pointer indexes.

Specialises in public-procurement journalism, including a standing series 'Významné zakázky' mapping planned major contracts per ministry, ÚOHS decisions on IT tenders (e.g. OKsystem vs DXC on IS DAV II), and price analyses done with Hlídač státu. Highest signal-per-article for A2 among Czech outlets.

Business weekly that scrutinises tender design — e.g. reporting a CZK 1.3bn justice-digitisation tender with an abnormally short bid window. Useful for the 'was this tender rigged/steered' angle that registers never show.

Czech IT-business news server reporting supplier switches on large state IT systems (e.g. Eviden/Atos taking the tax information system from IBM at ~CZK 1.8bn). Directly names winning vendors and contract values — core A2 material for vendor-landscape tracking.

The only dedicated Czech professional banking monthly (65-year lineage, formerly 'Hlas banky'); covers retail/investment banking trends, new products and banking technology aimed at senior management. Best single outlet for supplier/technology narratives inside Czech banks.

Transport trade server that reports fare-collection/ticketing tenders in detail — winning supplier, contract value, amendments, EU co-funding. Confirmed reporting on the Most/Litvínov ticketing system (Future/Herman technologies, CZK 40.7m ex-VAT). Transit ticketing is a major EMV-contactless payments channel in CZ.

source_subtype: investigative desk of national news portal
why_relevant: Largest Czech commercial investigative desk; breaks stories on rigged/contested public IT contracts and the people behind supplier firms. An author page gives a clean, stable feed of the team's output.

Subscription investigative daily; works from police/court documents on IT-procurement cases (e.g. the VZP raid, naming Total Service and Elso Philips Service as IT suppliers under investigation). Supplies named-actor detail that registers and press releases omit.

Public-service, free-to-read news and data-journalism site with per-bank tag pages (e.g. Komerční banka) and coverage of procurement raids. Free access makes it the practical substitute for paywalled investigative reporting.

National news agency's free public wire. Agency copy is the origin of most short Czech tender/award items later republished elsewhere, so it is the earliest and most citable timestamp for award announcements; ČTK also runs a paid protext/full-wire service.

Monthly trade magazine for retail, suppliers and retail technology. Covers merchant-side payment acceptance, terminal/POS deployments and digital-payment adoption — the demand side of acquiring deals that A2 tender data does not capture.

Logistics trade title; relevant to payments through last-mile and parcel-locker technology with integrated payment terminals (COD, card acceptance at boxes). Low tender density but useful for supplier names in self-service payment hardware.

Commercial spin-off of Hlídač státu selling multi-year price analyses of Czech ICT services derived from procurement data — the market's most extensive ICT price benchmark. Directly useful for pricing context on bank/state IT tenders.

Anti-corruption NGO documenting procurement cases and the functioning of ÚOHS itself (the regulator that rules on contested tenders). Media cite it heavily; its case pages point to the underlying tenders and actors.

Czech enterprise-IT monthly; issues carry dedicated banking-transformation features (banks as technology companies, digital payments, analytics, automation) that name platforms and integrators serving Czech banks.
Czech OCCRP partner covering organised crime, money laundering and opaque ownership. Relevant to A2 for beneficial-ownership checks on bidders and for AML/financial-crime angles touching banks.

Public broadcaster's economics desk reports award outcomes with values and winning suppliers (e.g. the building-authority IS contract at CZK 24m won by Servodata). Free, archived and citable — good corroboration layer for paywalled reporting.

High-volume regional/national daily; freely republishes and summarises procurement-scandal reporting originated by paywalled outlets, and covers municipal/regional tenders (transport, ticketing, municipal payment services) that national media skip.

source_name: Portál otevřených dat ČR / Národní katalog otevřených dat (NKOD) — data.gov.cz
why_relevant: National open data catalogue operated by Digitální a informační agentura (DIA). It is the master index of every dataset the Czech state publishes as open data, including public-procurement datasets (VVZ/ISVZ, Registr smluv, ÚOHS decisions, ARES). For an A2 tender scout it is the single entry point from which all other structured procurement datasets can be enumerated and their distribution URLs (CSV/XML/API) harvested via DCAT-AP metadata.

source_name: ISVZ — Informační systém o veřejných zakázkách, OpenData section (MMR)
why_relevant: MMR's analytical layer over the VVZ. Publishes an explicit OpenData section with procurement records from the Bulletin and electronic marketplaces in XML, XLS and CSV, refreshed monthly (15th, for the prior month), plus statistical outputs and the contracting-authority-profile validator. This is the cleanest bulk route to reconstruct historic Czech award series without scraping notice pages.

source_name: Registr smluv (ISRS) open data dumps — data.smlouvy.gov.cz
why_relevant: Act 340/2015 Sb. forces publication of contracts above CZK 50k excl. VAT by a broad set of public bodies, including state banks and public institutions. Monthly XML dumps (dump_<YYYY>_<MM>.xml) with an XSD carry the actual signed contract metadata — counterparty, value, effective date and often contract duration. This is the single best structured route to incumbent identity and contract expiry dates, i.e. the true re-tender trigger for the A2 workstream.

Documented machine interface to the contract register for querying/publishing records — an incremental alternative to full monthly dumps for near-real-time detection of newly signed banking/payments contracts.

source_name: EU Public Procurement Data Space (PPDS) / data.europa.eu curated TED CSV
why_relevant: PPDS aggregates TED plus a growing set of national procurement datasets with dashboards; data.europa.eu also hosts a curated TED CSV covering 2006-2023 with the core 'who bought what from whom, for how much' fields — an easy analytical backbone for long historic series. Czech national-level data did not appear among the nationally onboarded datasets in what I found, so CZ coverage here is via the TED layer.

source_name: Datlab s.r.o. — commercial tender database & Datlab Tenders API
why_relevant: Czech data company behind Opentender and vsechnyzakazky.cz; markets a cleaned supplier and tender-documentation database covering 50+ countries with supplier risk profiling. An API documentation space exists on Apiary (digiwhist.docs.apiary.io). The highest-quality commercial route to normalised CZ award history and supplier identity resolution, if budget allows.

Aggregates Czech contracts subject to the procurement act (excluding small-scale ones) from many contracting-authority profiles into one searchable index — useful to discover which authority profile a given banking/payments contract lives on, and to snowball into profile URLs that are otherwise hard to enumerate.
